classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that class totals may differ and explain why proportions give a fair comparison of the same homework-hours group.

content.prompt: A class survey asked how many hours per week students spend on homework. Discuss why using relative frequency is better than absolute frequency when comparing with another class.

answer.short: Relative frequencies compare the proportions of students in each class, which accounts for different class sizes.
answer.worked: For a given number or range of homework hours, divide the count in each class by that class’s total number of students. The resulting proportions are directly comparable. A larger class can have a higher count even when the same proportion of its students report those hours.
